actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined metabolic downregulation program with large effect sizes and FDR significance. WXS and CNV are not significant but do not actively contradict the identity. Per-set technical associations are not significant, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining this discovery-stage candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0002 shows moderate cross-modal support with significant CNV copy-number losses and nominal PBRM1 enrichment, plus RNA pathway upregulation. Per-set technical associations are not significant. Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. The candidate has a defensible molecular identity for downstream validation.

C0003 lacks coherent biological identity: only one RNA pathway is significant, WXS and CNV show no FDR-significant findings, and cross-modal consistency is weak with several patients having zero modality support. No positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge, and no extra evidence is available. The candidate is not sufficiently defensible for retention.

C0004 has no significant biological findings in any modality, with only nominal trends and wide confidence intervals. Cross-modal consistency is weak and internal structure is unstable (high PAC). No positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge, and no extra evidence is available. The candidate lacks a defensible identity for downstream validation.

C0005 is strongly confounded by technical factors: per-set tests show significant associations with CT manufacturer, scanner model, and reconstruction kernel. The set is primarily CT-driven (CT median silhouette 0.274) with no significant biological support in RNA, WXS, or CNV. The measured technical explanation plausibly dominates the identity evidence, so Drop is better supported than Accept.

C0006 has strong RNA-defined inflammatory/interferon program with large effect sizes and FDR significance, plus significant BAP1 mutation enrichment. Per-set technical associations are not significant, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. The candidate has a coherent molecular identity for downstream validation.
